key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows unexpectedly inverted elastic anisotropy and strong orientation-dependent yield onset, and these trends cannot be explained by simple cubic-elasticity or Schmid-factor/CRSS models alone.
engineering_relevance: For texture-engineered Ti-15Mo components, crystal orientation can shift stiffness and yielding enough to affect local deformation, damage initiation, and process design.
method: EBSD-guided nanoindentation on orientations near <111>, <124>, <011>, <023>, and <013>
Measured indentation modulus, hardness, strain-rate sensitivity, and yield-onset response
Used strain-rate-jump tests to estimate activation volume and infer deformation mechanism classes
evidence_signal: Across the tested orientations, modulus varied by about 10%, yield onset by 41%, and hardness by 6.6%, while activation volumes of 18–31 b^3 suggested kink-pair-nucleation-controlled plasticity.
watch_item: The proposed role of retained athermal ω is plausible but indirect, so confirming the mechanism would require complementary phase-sensitive in situ measurements.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
